**Metabolomics Pathway Analysis Narrative**

The RaMP hypergeometric enrichment analysis of the 10 differentially-abundant metabolites returned a highly coherent signal: the top five candidate pathways are all SMPDB inflammation-modulation pathways, all sharing the **Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (SMP00075)** as their biochemical core. The two highest-confidence hits are the **Celecoxib Action Pathway** (SMP00096; FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 469.9) and the **Ibuprofen Action Pathway** (SMP00086; FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 450.3), each annotated with six of the ten input compounds.

**Key driver compounds** are the oxygenated arachidonate derivatives: 8(S)-HPETE (C14823), 16(R)-HETE (C14778), 19(S)-HETE (C14749), and 11,12,15-THETA (C14782). These four metabolites — all confirmed members of Arachidonic Acid Metabolism — collectively anchor the enrichment signal and reflect perturbed cytochrome-P450 (CYP) and/or lipoxygenase (LOX) branches of the pathway. Thromboxane A2 (C02198), a well-established prostanoid synthesized via the cyclooxygenase (COX) route, is also present and belongs to the same SMPDB inflammatory-action maps, consistent with a broad disruption of eicosanoid flux rather than a single enzymatic arm.

**Biological significance.** Arachidonic acid metabolism sits at the nexus of inflammation, vascular tone, and platelet aggregation. The simultaneous elevation of multiple HETEs and HPETEs alongside thromboxane suggests the treatment may act on or perturb both the LOX and COX arms — a pattern reported in contexts of NSAID exposure, oxidative stress, or cytokine-mediated phospholipase activation. S-Adenosylmethionine (C00019) adds a methyl-donor dimension that can influence eicosanoid-regulatory enzymes through epigenetic or post-translational modification. The absence of direct KEGG-graph connectivity between 8(S)-HPETE and thromboxane within the resolution budget indicates they arise from parallel, not sequential, branches of the arachidonate cascade.

In summary, the data most parsimoniously reflect a **global disturbance of arachidonic acid metabolism**, with CYP/LOX-derived HETEs and COX-derived thromboxane as the primary driver metabolites, consistent with an inflammatory or anti-inflammatory stimulus that broadly reshapes eicosanoid homeostasis.
